clue.text: Saturnine doctor got out of bed

blocks.note: MO is a Medical Officer, a standard crossword doctor
past tense of rise, to get up in the morning

explanation.surface: A gloomy physician hauls himself out of bed in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine describes a gloomy, sullen temperament, and morose is a direct synonym for that sour mood.

clue.text: Details of road turned up in time

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top, so backwards
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the A1 is the Great North Road, the 1 read as the letter I
a minute is a unit of time

explanation.surface: Particulars of a road that was dug up in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, from London to Edinburgh, and its digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Minutiae are small, precise or trivial points, which is what details means in the plural.

clue.text: Recompenses rising artist with a shilling

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read upwards, so backwards

blocks.note: a drawer is one who draws
s is the abbreviation for an old British shilling

explanation.surface: Payment to an up-and-coming painter of one shilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising artist' suggests an up-and-coming talent; it is a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rewards and recompenses are both nouns for payments or returns given in exchange for service.

clue.text: Appearing in burlesque, am I shocked, easily shocked?

indicators.note: something appearing in the words is sitting inside them, waiting to be read off

blocks.note: the letters run across the words, ignoring spaces and punctuation

explanation.surface: A spectator at a saucy variety show wonders if they are offended, being a prude.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue prints shocked twice: the first one lends its opening two letters to the run, and the second belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeamish person is quickly disgusted or upset, so easily shocked is a fair description of them.

clue.text: Be successful in repair

blocks.note: first meaning: to prosper and rise in the world
second meaning: to put right damage or a loss

explanation.surface: Someone thriving in the business of mending things.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to succeed in life and to compensate for or fix damage done.

clue.text: A charge that is. I found, novel for author

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take on a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A detective says 'there's the charge, I've worked it out', in a crime novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' fits the writer of detective novels, which hides its job as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie was the English writer of detective novels featuring Poirot and Miss Marple.

clue.text: Take part in record

blocks.note: first meaning: to join a competition
second meaning: to write down in a register or ledger

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like playing on a recording; 'record' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to sign up for a contest and to write an item into a log or account book.

clue.text: Ishmael not included with the players

blocks.note: left out, not in
the cast is the company of actors in a play

explanation.surface: A man called Ishmael was left out of the acting company.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Ishmael was driven into the wilderness, so his name stands for any outcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Ishmael, son of Abraham and Hagar, was banished, and his name became a byword for a rejected person.

clue.text: Sorted out some 12 in the South West

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters before it are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has arranged a patch of land in the south-west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorted out' looks like one phrase; split it so Sorted is the fodder. 12 is TERRAIN, so 'some 12' is a piece of land. DORSET is a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorset is an English county in the South West, so it is a portion of land in that region.

clue.text: Nearing journey's end, in more than one sense

definitions.text: Nearing journey's end, in more than one sense

blocks.note: the surface reading: a traveller on the final stages of a trip
the setter's reading: the journey is also life itself, so the phrase means close to collapse or death

explanation.walkthrough: A journey is made of stages called legs, so the final stages are literal; the idiom means worn out or dying.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone exhausted or near death, and the clue adds the literal travelling sense.

clue.text: Mint money for island

blocks.note: in mint condition means brand new
a guinea is an old British gold coin worth 21 shillings

explanation.surface: Freshly struck coins paid out to buy an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mint' looks like a verb about making coins, which suits 'money', but it is an adjective meaning brand new.
explanation.definitionFit: New Guinea is a large island in the western Pacific, north of Australia, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: Murphy, the adviser to Eire's Republican leaders

indicators.note: leaders are the ones at the front, so only the opening letter of each word counts

blocks.note: the initial letters of these five words

explanation.surface: An Irishman named Murphy serves as counsellor to the heads of Ireland's Republican party.
explanation.walkthrough: Murphy looks like a person's name, but it is slang for a potato, from its association with Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Murphy and tater are both informal slang terms for a potato, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Trainer sorted out the lie of the land

indicators.note: something sorted out is put into a different order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A racehorse trainer has worked out how the course runs before the race.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is the physical features of a stretch of ground, which is what the lie of the land describes.

clue.text: In this place, see concealed pot plants

indicators.note: something concealed is hidden inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: here means in this place
to pot game is to shoot it, which is also to bag it

explanation.surface: Look: in this spot someone has hidden cannabis among the greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot' suggests a plant pot or cannabis, but here it is the verb for shooting game, as is bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbage is herbaceous vegetation collectively, especially grass and leafy growth, so it stands for plants in general.

clue.text: Very musical, when it gets one

blocks.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
it is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Something becomes highly tuneful once it receives a single addition.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the definition as 'very, in music': assai is the Italian tempo marking, as in allegro assai.
explanation.definitionFit: Assai is an Italian performance direction meaning very or extremely, used to intensify a tempo marking.

clue.text: Pledge protection

blocks.note: first meaning: something deposited as a guarantee for a loan
second meaning: safety from harm or danger

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a promise of protection; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers collateral given against a debt and also the state of being safe or guarded.

clue.text: Music fabulous bird brings right into prominence

indicators.note: brings means takes along, so what follows is joined on after
into puts one piece inside another

blocks.note: the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend
a knoll is a small rounded hill, a prominence
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A mythical bird makes a tune famous by setting it right.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside KNOLL, after the N. 'Prominence' looks like fame, but it is a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock'n'roll is the popular music style of the 1950s, so it is an example of music.

clue.text: Feeling ecstatic - that's not heartless

indicators.note: heartless means losing the middle, so the central letter is dropped

blocks.note: sent is old slang for thrilled or carried away
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation id est, that is
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone feels delighted, though not lacking a heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' stands for 'that is', i.e.; heartless strips the O from NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentient means able to perceive and experience sensations, so it is the adjective feeling.

clue.text: Broadcast about the parade

blocks.note: on can mean about, as in a talk on history
taken as written
to parade an opinion is to air it, show it off

explanation.surface: Television coverage concerning a procession.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme that is being broadcast is transmitting live, which is what the phrase means.

clue.text: Removing the bottom of Venetian blind is simplicity itself

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom is the final letter, and removing it drops that letter
blind suggests stumbling without direction, so the letters move into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fixing a window blind by taking off its lowest slat is child's play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Venetian blind' looks like one window fitting; Venetian is the fodder and blind the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is innocent lack of worldliness, the quality of unsophisticated simplicity itself.

clue.text: Many long for a hiding place

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
to ache for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: Plenty of people yearn for somewhere to hide.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a secret store or the concealed spot where supplies or valuables are kept.

clue.text: Giving a name to business

blocks.note: first meaning: naming someone or something
second meaning: a vocation or trade

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like naming a company; split it after 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a participle meaning naming and a noun meaning one's profession or occupation.

clue.text: A group of notes sounded in harmony

indicators.note: sounded means spoken, so the answer matches the pronunciation of the phrase

blocks.note: a chord is several notes played together

explanation.surface: Several notes played together ring out in tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Accord means agreement or concord, a state of harmony between people.

clue.text: A game creature

blocks.note: first meaning: the bat-and-ball sport
second meaning: a chirping insect

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as 'a game creature', a brave or hunted animal; split it after 'game'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the English summer sport played with bat and ball and a leaping, chirping insect.

clue.text: King and royal mistress make an announcement

blocks.note: K is king in chess notation
Nell Gwyn was the mistress of Charles II

explanation.surface: A monarch and his lover issue a public statement.
explanation.definitionFit: A knell is a bell rung solemnly to announce a death, so it is a mournful announcement.

clue.text: Celebrate with hired clothing

blocks.note: to sing of something is to celebrate it
let means rented out, as a flat is let

explanation.surface: Party in a rented outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: A singlet is a sleeveless vest, an undershirt or athletics top.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless garment worn on the upper body, so it is an example of clothing.

clue.text: Orders sweetheart stout

blocks.note: OBE is the Order of the British Empire; several are OBEs
the heart of sweet is its middle letter, a standard crossword trick

explanation.surface: Someone instructs their darling, a plump one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' looks like a lover but splits into sweet plus heart, the middle letter of sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout describes a heavily built, fat person, and obese is a stronger synonym for being very overweight.

clue.text: Make an example of me? I 'ope it's not right

indicators.note: letters that are not right are wrong, so they must be put into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, the dropped aitch included

explanation.surface: A Cockney worries that being held up as a warning to others would be unfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make an example of' suggests punishing someone, but here it means to be the typical example of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To epitomise something is to be a perfect example of it, embodying its typical qualities.

clue.text: Contestant is after two lines in a song

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other, so the order of joining is reversed from the clue
in puts the joined pieces inside the other word

blocks.note: the start of DUET, a song for two
L is the abbreviation for line, so two of them
taken as written
the end of DUET, closing round the inserted letters

explanation.surface: A competitor shows up a couple of lines into a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A song' is split around the other pieces: a duet is a song for two singers, apt for a contest between two.
explanation.definitionFit: A duellist fights a duel, a formal combat between two opponents, so he is a contestant.

clue.text: Burning land

blocks.note: first meaning: on fire
second meaning: to come down and settle, as a bird does

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as scorched earth, but 'land' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for something on fire and a verb for descending to settle on a surface.
